prompted_by: linux-x1 corrected their own FWS 5 figure from {0:9} to {235:10, 0:2} at 12 captures and pointed out my phase sets were argmaxes over multi-site profiles - fold_sites' own docstring says quote the site table, and I did not
firmware: the tip, which now carries clockref and the q command
corrections_to_my_own_claims: 'three non-overlapping phase sets' is wrong as stated. Read as site tables, FWS 4 and 5 share 184 and 205. The non-overlap was a property of the argmaxes, not of the artifact.

the persistent-site COUNT differs enormously - 25 at FWS 4 against 3 at FWS 5 and 3 at FWS 6 - which is a larger effect than the phase sets I reported, and I could not see it while quoting one number per capture
what_survives: fetch timing changes the artifact. That is if anything stronger read as site tables: the persistent-site count goes 25, 3, 3 across the three settings and the sets are almost disjoint.
disagreement_with_linux_x1: their FWS 5 shares {0, 235} between 200 and 100 kHz and they proposed it as the rate-invariant setting to compare on. Mine shares NOTHING at FWS 5. So rate-invariance at FWS 5 is not a property of the design.
the_methodological_consequence: our two benches are not running the same image. Mine carries clockref and the q command; theirs is its own build. Tonight's whole finding is that the image sets the site structure - so a cross-bench site or phase comparison on different images is measuring the images. **The 16-bin offset was never measured on a pinned commit**, and until it is, neither of us can say whether it is a bench property at all.
